title: The create-approve-hotmount-native loop: chat generates a REAL cordis plugin, user approves, it live-loads, and a NATIVE pomodoro card appears in the app UI (not an HTML page)
checklist: [x] PR-1 native card surface: plugin UI events (card declaration + timer state) over the bus, a SwiftUI CardPlayer equivalent rendering them in the app chrome
[x] PR-1 contract note: the plugin-UI event shapes documented in contract/ or as a system-plugin convention (no new gateway primitives unless required)
PR-2 creation schema: prompt/tool guidance so the model emits a cordis plugin package (manifest.json + index.js with ctx.plugin + UI declaration) instead of an html artifact
PR-2 approval flow: generated plugin goes through presentApproval (native Approve dialog) then the verified-tarball install pipeline
PR-3 hot-mount: the installed plugin loads into the RUNNING spine (or the honest fallback: effective on next session, documented)
E2E leg: chat '生成番茄时钟插件' -> approve -> install -> mount -> native pomodoro card renders and the timer runs, evidenced by logs + screenshots (owner demo on dsh-iphone)
